title: Goal identity for hooks is bound by pane env or by cwd, and neither works for a reused session
evidence: 01d-goal-hooks.md:40-49 (Claude/Codex hooks gate on FLEET_GOAL_ID in the pane env; Muse gates on a cwd/session_id registry); 03c-goals.md:88-91 (FLEET_GOAL_ID is set only in the `ensure_window` step); 03c-goals.md:84-87 and command_goal.proto:109-113 (StartGoal can instead reuse an existing pane, so no ensure_window runs); 01-agent-capabilities.md:289-292 (E9 mapping is learned from hooks recording the session id against FLEET_PANE_KEY); events.proto:207-216 and snapshot.proto:194-214 (goal_id is carried on HarnessHookEvent, GoalState, PaneExited and PromptDetected with no stated source); 01d-goal-hooks.md:263-267 (open question about the registry only covers a goal that cd's away).
problem: Reuse of an available session is the steady-state dispatch path. A running harness process cannot gain a new env var, so in a reused pane FLEET_GOAL_ID is either absent (a session the developer marked available) or still the previous goal's id (a fleet-started session). Claude and Codex hooks therefore stay inert (no Stop guard, no E8 events), or events are attributed to the wrong goal. SessionStart already fired before the goal existed, so E9 (harness session id per pane) is never learned either. The Muse cwd registry has no lifecycle (when entries are removed, what happens when two goals share a checkout, reuse in REPO_DRIVER mode where the registered path is the main checkout and would capture every Muse session the developer runs there) and no wire representation, so the hub cannot see or reconcile it after an agent state loss.
fix: Decide that goal attribution is the agent's registry for all three harnesses, written by StartGoal before type_goal (new step register_goal) and removed on DONE/CLEARED/MERGED, pane exit or prune. Key it by (pane_key, worktree path, harness_session_id), learning the session id from the first UserPromptSubmit/PreToolUse hook after registration. FLEET_GOAL_ID stays a fast path for new windows only. Add additive wire fields: a goal_binding source enum plus harness_session_id on PaneHarnessSession, and registered goals in Snapshot for hub reconciliation. Document registry behaviour for two goals sharing a checkout and for REPO_DRIVER mode (path is the main checkout), rather than hard-refusing it.
verify: Confirmed. 01d-goal-hooks.md:40-49 binds Claude/Codex hooks to FLEET_GOAL_ID in the pane env and Muse to a cwd registry. 03c-goals.md:84-91 sets FLEET_GOAL_ID only in ensure_window, and StartGoal.reuse_pane (command_goal.proto:109-113) skips that step. A running harness process cannot gain a new env var, so a reused pane has no goal id (marked-available developer session) or the previous goal's id. E9 (01-agent-capabilities.md:289-292) is learned from SessionStart against FLEET_PANE_KEY, which also predates the goal. grep of FLEET_GOAL_ID across docs/api finds no reuse-path handling. 01d:263-267 open question covers only a goal that cd's away. The Muse registry has no lifecycle and no wire field (snapshot.proto:115-140 has no binding). Reuse is the steady-state dispatch path (03c:70-71), so this blocks the central flow.
resolution: Goal identity is the agent's goal registry for all harnesses: new GoalRegistration, Snapshot.goal_registry, Event.goal_registry, RegisterGoal/ReleaseGoal, StartGoal step register_goal, TmuxPane.goal, PaneHarnessSession.goal/binding; FLEET_GOAL_ID is only a new-window fast path. Lifecycle, hook lookup order, two-goals-one-checkout and REPO_DRIVER rules in 02h; 01d and ADR 0019 item 17 updated.

title: Session reuse has no check that the pane is in the goal's repo or worktree
evidence: snapshot.proto:115-140 (TmuxPane has no cwd or repo); command_goal.proto:29-74 and :107-123 (GoalSpec.workdir, branch and worktree_mode, plus StartGoal.reuse_pane); 03c-goals.md:70-71 (planning rule: reuse any available session of the same harness on the machine); 03c-goals.md:84-87 (pick_session re-checks only idle, available and empty input line); 03c-goals.md:316 ('a session that was reused is left alone'); 01-agent-capabilities.md:293-306 (E11); status.proto:75-168 (no reason code for a workdir mismatch).
problem: The goal's worktree is ensured first, then a pane is reused whose harness process is fixed in a different cwd (typically the previous goal's worktree, possibly another repo). Claude and Muse cannot change directory (Codex has /cd). The goal would run in the wrong checkout, against the wrong branch, and Muse's cwd registry (01d) would not match. Neither PreflightResult.would_reuse nor any ReasonCode expresses this, and the hub cannot filter candidates because the agent never reports pane cwd.
fix: Add TmuxPane.current_path (tmux pane_current_path) plus a normalized RepoRef and worktree_path when under an allowed root, and REASON_CODE_SESSION_WORKDIR_MISMATCH enforced by pick_session and Preflight. Decide explicitly: reuse only when the pane's cwd is the goal's repo (worktree per session, branch switched in place), or only for harnesses that can /cd. Update planning rule 3 in 03c to match on repo.
verify: Confirmed. TmuxPane (snapshot.proto:115-140) has no cwd, repo or worktree path. 03c-goals.md:70-71 prefers any available session of the same harness on the machine with no repo match. pick_session (03c:84-87, diagram 03c:38) re-checks only idle, available_for_work and an empty input line. status.proto has no workdir-mismatch reason and PreflightResult.would_reuse cannot express it. A reused pane's harness process stays in its original cwd, so the goal would run in the wrong checkout or branch and the hub cannot filter candidates. This forces a decision on per-session vs per-goal worktrees (EnsureWorktree/PruneWorktree semantics) before implementation.
resolution: TmuxPane.workdir (PaneWorkdir{current_path, repo, checkout_path, is_worktree, branch, dirty}) plus hub Pane.workdir; reuse only when the pane is a clean checkout of the goal's repo, with REASON_CODE_SESSION_WORKDIR_MISMATCH and CHECKOUT_DIRTY from pick_session and Preflight.reuse_pane; planning rule 3 in 03c matches on repo (02h, Reuse).

title: The developer-keystroke signal that suppresses nudges and drives the typing banner has no wire carrier for goal panes
evidence: 03c-goals.md:272-273 and :367 (human_at_keyboard_until is set 10 min after AvailabilityChanged{reason='keystroke'}); 03-workflows.md:331; ui-contract-map.md:104 (banner 'you're typing into a running goal'); harness.proto:133-142 and 01-agent-capabilities.md:293-306 (Availability.idle requires 'no goal is active', so a goal pane is never idle); events.proto:229-238 (AvailabilityChanged is a from/to of Availability); events.proto:163-169 and snapshot.proto:115-140 (ActivityTransition and TmuxPane track output only, there is no last_input_at).
problem: A goal pane is never idle by definition, so no idle-to-busy transition, and therefore no 'keystroke' AvailabilityChanged, is ever emitted for it. The hub's rule to hold off nudges, goal control and the banner has no input. An Esc interrupt is also a keystroke; because the rule has no input, a goal the developer just interrupted looks like 'idle at ready prompt with WORKING line' and gets the corrective nudge (03c:284-296). tmux control mode also does not expose client input, so how the agent observes it is not stated.
fix: Add an additive per-pane input-activity signal: TmuxPane.last_input_at plus a COALESCE event (for example HumanInput{pane, at}), rate-limited, with the detection method specified (tmux client_activity polling or similar). Reword 03c:272 and 03-workflows.md:331 to consume it instead of AvailabilityChanged{keystroke}.
verify: Confirmed. Availability.idle requires no active goal (harness.proto:133-135, 01-agent-capabilities.md:293-295), so a goal pane is never idle and no idle-to-busy 'keystroke' AvailabilityChanged is emitted for it. Yet 03c-goals.md:272-273 and 03-workflows.md:331 derive human_at_keyboard_until and the nudge/goal-control suppression from exactly that event. TmuxPane has no last_input_at and no input event exists (grep for keystroke/last_input/HumanInput finds only the AvailabilityChanged reason string and the terminal stream). How the agent observes developer input is unstated. An Esc interrupt with no signal feeds the one-nudge rule (03c:284-296).
resolution: TmuxPane.last_input_time and Event.pane_input (PaneInput, COALESCE, at most one per 10 s) carry developer input on goal panes, with the detection method (tmux client_activity polling) in 02h; 03c, 03-workflows and 03f consume it instead of AvailabilityChanged{keystroke}.

title: Interrupt and pause have no wire representation, although 01d says they are reported as a HarnessCondition
evidence: 01d-goal-hooks.md:116-127 ('The agent reports HarnessCondition (E12) and the hub opens a Triage item goal interrupted'); harness.proto:199-213 (HarnessConditionKind: PROVIDER_ERROR, RATE_LIMITED, USAGE_LIMIT, SIGN_IN_REQUIRED, NETWORK, OTHER); events.proto:197-204 (HookEventKind has no INTERRUPT, though Codex's Interrupt hook is the only hook signal); harness.proto:145-155 (GoalLineState has no PAUSED); 03c-goals.md:284-296 (idle with a WORKING line triggers the one-nudge rule); 01d-goal-hooks.md:23-24 ('never resume a goal the developer interrupted').
problem: An interrupted Claude goal ('Goal active', goal file still WORKING), a paused Codex goal, and a Muse 'goal paused by interrupt' are all indistinguishable on the wire from a stopped-without-DONE goal. The hub's nudge rule would type 'Your goal is still active. Continue' into a goal the developer deliberately stopped, which is the opposite of 01d. A native-/goal achieved or cleared state also has no field. The agent can only fall into OTHER or UNSPECIFIED.
fix: Add HARNESS_CONDITION_KIND_GOAL_INTERRUPTED (cleared when the goal runs again) and optionally HOOK_EVENT_KIND_INTERRUPT. Make 03c's stopped-without-DONE rule suppress on an open interrupted condition and map it to GOAL_PHASE_PAUSED with the 01d triage item. GOAL_LINE_STATE_PAUSED is optional.
verify: Confirmed. 01d-goal-hooks.md:116-127 says the agent reports an interrupt as a HarnessCondition (E12) and the hub opens a Triage item, and that nothing resumes automatically. HarnessConditionKind (harness.proto:199-213) has only PROVIDER_ERROR, RATE_LIMITED, USAGE_LIMIT, SIGN_IN_REQUIRED, NETWORK, OTHER, and HookEventKind (events.proto:197-204) has no INTERRUPT (raw_event_name exists for unmapped kinds, which softens the hook half). GoalLineState has no PAUSED, and GOAL_PHASE_PAUSED (hub goal.proto:36-37) is set only by operator, review-loop cap or reserve rule. The stopped-without-DONE rule (03c-goals.md:284-296) suppresses only on provider_condition, prompt_pending and human_at_keyboard, so a developer-interrupted Claude goal (Stop does not fire on Esc, 01d:116-120) would be nudged 'continue', contradicting 01d and the product ground rule.
resolution: New HarnessConditionKind GOAL_INTERRUPTED and GOAL_PAUSED with HarnessCondition.pause_cause, and HOOK_EVENT_KIND_INTERRUPT; 03c suppresses the nudge on an open condition and maps it to PAUSED{OWNER_AT_MACHINE} with a GOAL_PAUSED triage item. GOAL_LINE_STATE_PAUSED not added: the goal file still says WORKING.

title: The hub is told to check /goal subcommand support before sending, but the agent never reports it
evidence: 01b-harness-commands.md:116-117 ('the hub never sends one that isn't listed'); hub/v1/goal.proto:224-226 (ControlGoal 'fails with GOAL_SUBCOMMAND_UNSUPPORTED before sending'); hub/v1/goal.proto:195-212 (pause is Interrupt for Claude and /goal pause for Codex and Muse; resume is typed `continue` for Claude and /goal resume for Codex and Muse); harness.proto:32-46 (CatalogEntry has only name and class); snapshot.proto:82-108 (HarnessInfo has no goal-control field); 02-contracts.md:297 (capability names include `goal.start` and a stale `goal.stop`, none for goal control).
problem: Whether a harness version supports pause, resume, edit and clear, and whether pause means a subcommand or Interrupt, is hard-coded hub-side per harness name. A harness update that adds `/goal pause` to Claude, or drops one in Codex, is discovered only after a failed command, and the Claude resume text `continue` is an unversioned hub constant. The 'before sending' promise cannot be met.
fix: Either add an additive HarnessInfo goal-control summary (supported subcommands, pause/resume mode, resume text) filled by the adapter per version, or reword 01b:116-117 and goal.proto:224-226 to say the failure comes from the agent and the hub falls back. Remove `goal.stop` from 02-contracts.md:297 either way.
verify: The gap exists: 01b-harness-commands.md:116-117 says the adapter records supported subcommands and the hub never sends an unlisted one, and hub goal.proto:224-226 promises GOAL_SUBCOMMAND_UNSUPPORTED 'before sending'. But CatalogEntry (harness.proto:32-46) is only name and class, and HarnessInfo (snapshot.proto:82-108) has no subcommand field. Severity is overstated: a reactive path already exists (02-contracts.md:145 G4 returns GOAL_SUBCOMMAND_UNSUPPORTED from the agent; 03c-goals.md:371 falls back to Interrupt), and pre-send detection is an optimization. The stale `goal.stop` capability name (02-contracts.md:297; StopGoal removed per 02-contracts.md:469, command.proto:45) is confirmed.
resolution: HarnessInfo.goal_control (GoalControl: subcommands, pause_mode, resume_mode, resume_text, limit_resume_verified) in type/v1/harness.proto, shown as MachineHarness.goal_control; the hub keeps no per-harness table (01b, 03c, 02h). goal.stop was already removed from 02-contracts.

title: SendKeys is used for nudges, Claude resume and limit-wait resume, but its gating is tied to prompt answering and it lacks an idle check
evidence: command_tmux.proto:119-128 (SendKeys has only answering_prompt and require_empty_input_line); command_tmux.proto:168-171 and 01-agent-capabilities.md:337-338 (RunHarnessCommand requires 'ready pattern showing, never into a running turn'); 01-agent-capabilities.md:284-285 and snapshot.proto:97-98 ('send-to-pane is enabled only once prompt detection is verified'); design.md:416-417 (Codex and Muse waiting detection still open); 03c-goals.md:290-296 (corrective nudge via SendKeys for every harness); 02-contracts.md:364-366 (limit-wait resume `SendKeys{'continue'}` for Claude); hub/v1/session.proto:156-165.
problem: One untyped command serves three purposes with different safety needs. require_empty_input_line does not imply the harness is idle: in a running Claude turn the input line is empty and typed text is queued as the next message. If the send-to-pane gate is applied to SendKeys generally, nudges and resume are blocked for Codex and Muse until prompt detection is verified, although they depend on the READY parser, not PROMPT. If it is not applied, the gate protects nothing. 'Typed commands only' is weakest exactly where hub-authored free text is typed.
fix: Doc-first: state that the E6 verification gate applies only when answering_prompt is set and that text sends are gated by ParserFeature.READY. If wanted, add an additive require_ready_prompt flag on SendKeys (PANE_BUSY otherwise). A separate SubmitPrompt kind is optional.
verify: Partly confirmed. SendKeys (command_tmux.proto:119-128) has only answering_prompt and require_empty_input_line, with no ready-prompt check, whereas RunHarnessCommand requires the ready pattern (command_tmux.proto:168-171). 01-agent-capabilities.md:284-285 says send-to-pane is disabled until prompt detection is verified and design.md:416-417 leaves Codex/Muse waiting detection open, so it is unstated whether nudges and the Claude limit-wait resume (02-contracts.md:364-366) are gated by E6 or only by READY. The input line is empty during a running Claude turn, so require_empty_input_line is not an idle check. Impact is small: the hub decides on an idle+ready transition first and a stray nudge becomes a queued message, so this is a clarification rather than a refactor driver. Hub SendKeysRequest (session.proto:156-165) mirrors the same fields.
resolution: SendKeys.purpose (SendKeysPurpose: PROMPT_ANSWER, GOAL_NUDGE, GOAL_RESUME, OPERATOR_TEXT) replaces require_empty_input_line; the E6 gate applies only to prompt answers, text sends need the READY parser, ready pattern showing and an empty input line (PANE_BUSY). Hub SendKeysRequest is OPERATOR_TEXT; 02g matrix rows split per purpose.

title: SetSessionAvailability addresses a tmux session but availability is a per-pane fact
evidence: command_tmux.proto:192-200 (SetSessionAvailability{SessionTarget session}); snapshot.proto:135 (TmuxPane.availability) and events.proto:229-238 (AvailabilityChanged.pane); 01-agent-capabilities.md:264-269 (windows are named by purpose, e.g. `codex prompt 1`, `claude w2`, `btop`, in one session); 01-agent-capabilities.md:297-300 (the developer marks 'it' available); hub/v1/session.proto:90 (sessions hold several windows and panes).
problem: A developer's tmux session usually holds several windows (several harnesses, btop). Marking the session cannot say which pane to treat as free capacity, and a mark on a session with two Claude panes is ambiguous. The spec also does not say where the mark persists (agent state across restart, pane respawn, tmux server restart changing server_start_id) or who re-asserts it on reconnect, though principle 1 puts desired state on the hub.
fix: Make the target oneof {SessionTarget session; PaneKey pane} (prefer pane) on both the agent command and the hub API. Specify that the agent persists marks in its state dir keyed by pane key and server_start_id, drops them when the pane dies, and reports them in TmuxPane.availability on every snapshot so the hub can re-send missing ones.
verify: Confirmed. SetSessionAvailability targets a SessionTarget (command_tmux.proto:192-200; hub SetSessionAvailabilityRequest session.proto:220-225) while availability lives per pane (TmuxPane.availability snapshot.proto:135, AvailabilityChanged.pane events.proto:229-238). Windows hold mixed purposes (01-agent-capabilities.md:264-269), so marking a session cannot identify the pane to use. The hub keeps available_for_work per session (03d-triage-sessions-logs.md:192). Where the mark persists across agent restart, tmux restart (server_start_id) or pane respawn is unspecified; 03d:205 says only that the command is declarative. Changing the target shape is cheapest before implementation.
resolution: SetSessionAvailability renamed SetPaneAvailability and addresses a PaneKey (agent command, hub RPC, OperationKind); reason is the enum AvailabilityReason. The agent persists marks per pane key in its state dir, drops them with the pane and reports them in TmuxPane.availability so the hub re-sends missing ones (02h, 03d).

title: The StartGoal composite step list and its retry/idempotency classification omit steps that GoalSpec and 01d require
evidence: command.proto:96-98 and 03c-goals.md:82-91 (steps: preflight, ensure_worktree, pick_session, ensure_window, wait_ready, type_goal, confirm_goal_file); command_goal.proto:56-69 (model, effort, fresh_context via /model, /effort, /clear); 01d-goal-hooks.md:103-109 (agent writes the initial goal file just before type_goal); 01d-goal-hooks.md:44-49 (registry write at StartGoal); 01-agent-capabilities.md:412 and 346-360 (goal panes are always log-captured, G3 text does not mention model/effort/clear); 02-contracts.md:205-210 (crash-resume treats only preflight, worktree and window as declarative); status.proto:75-168 and :136-148 (no reason for an unavailable model or effort).
problem: Typed steps (`/model`, `/effort`, `/clear`), the goal-file write, goal registration and starting pipe-pane capture are real side effects with different idempotency, but they are not named, have no failure reason codes, and are not classified for restart. Per-step retry policy in 03c:117-126 is keyed on step names that do not cover them. A crash after `/clear` and before type_goal, or between writing the goal file and typing, has undefined behaviour.
fix: Doc plus additive reason codes: list the full step sequence (preflight, ensure_worktree, write_goal_file, register_goal, start_log_capture, pick_session/ensure_window, wait_ready, set_model, set_effort, fresh_context, type_goal, confirm_goal_file) with a restart class per step. Treat fresh_context as non-idempotent. Add REASON_CODE_MODEL_NOT_AVAILABLE and REASON_CODE_EFFORT_NOT_SUPPORTED. Update the 03c retry table and the 02-contracts.md:205 resume rule.
verify: Confirmed gap, severity lowered. GoalSpec has model, effort and fresh_context (command_goal.proto:56-69, typed via /model, /effort, /clear), 01d-goal-hooks.md:103-109 has the agent write the goal file just before type_goal, and 01d:44-49 has a registry write. The step lists at 03c-goals.md:82-91 and command.proto CommandProgress.step comment do not name them (the proto comment says 'e.g.', so it is not exhaustive). The crash-resume rule at 02-contracts.md:205-210 classifies only preflight, worktree and window as declarative, so a crash after /clear (destructive) or after the goal-file write has no defined behaviour. status.proto has no reason for an unavailable model or effort (only FRESH_CONTEXT_NOT_ALLOWED at :146-148). Fixable by additive reason codes and doc edits, with no wire refactor.
resolution: StartGoal now has 14 named steps (preflight, pick_session, prepare_branch, ensure_worktree, ensure_window, register_goal, start_log_capture, wait_ready, set_model, set_effort, clear_context, write_goal_file, type_goal, confirm_goal_file), each with a restart class and failure reasons; clear_context and type_goal are non-idempotent (02h table, command_goal.proto, 02-contracts composite paragraph, 03c retry table).

title: Hook trust is a Codex-only bool with no unknown state, and several contract names have no capability behind them
evidence: harness.proto:56-58 (trust_pending 'Codex only'); 01d-goal-hooks.md:86-97 (Muse needs the same approval, `muse plugins approve`); events.proto:207-216 (HarnessHookEvent has no stop-guard decision or stop_hook_active, though 01d:18-22 says the guard 'refuses and escalates'); agent.proto:141 (CONNECT_REASON_HUB_REQUESTED, no hub message that requests a reconnect); events.proto:203 (HOOK_EVENT_KIND_GOAL_WRITTEN, but 01d:106-109 says the agent writes the goal file and hooks only read it); 02-contracts.md:297 (capability `goal.stop`); command_tmux.proto:135-143 and 01-agent-capabilities.md:158 (ResumeArgs use `--last`, RespawnPane carries no harness session id); snapshot.proto:159 and streams/LogStreamKey (agent cannot fill session_id for the developer's own sessions).
problem: proto3 bool false reads as 'trusted' when the agent cannot determine trust. The Triage item needs the harness-specific approve command, which the wire does not name. Stop-guard blocks cannot be audited or distinguished from a guard that never fires, which 03c:284-287 treats as a finding. Respawning with `--last` can resume the wrong conversation when several sessions share a cwd, though E9 already knows the session id. A log stream for a developer session has an empty session_id and must be keyed by pane.
fix: Cleanup items. Fix the trust_pending comment (Codex and Muse) and optionally make trust a tri-state enum. Delete or define HOOK_EVENT_KIND_GOAL_WRITTEN and CONNECT_REASON_HUB_REQUESTED. Optionally add HarnessHookEvent.decision and an optional harness_session_id on RespawnPane and EnsureWindow. Leave the LogStreamKey item as a doc note.
verify: Mostly confirmed but low value as a bundle. harness.proto:56-58 says trust_pending is 'Codex only' while 01d-goal-hooks.md:93-95 reuses it for Muse (stale comment, and a bool has no 'unknown' state). HOOK_EVENT_KIND_GOAL_WRITTEN (events.proto:203) has no producer because 01d:103-109 has the agent write the goal file. CONNECT_REASON_HUB_REQUESTED (agent.proto:141) has no hub message that requests a reconnect (grep finds only the enum). RespawnPane (command_tmux.proto:137-143) carries no harness session id while resume uses `--last` (01-agent-capabilities.md:158), which can pick the wrong conversation. HarnessHookEvent (events.proto:207-216) has no decision or stop_hook_active field. The LogStreamKey session_id point is weak: snapshot.proto:159 says session_id is empty for the developer's own sessions, but 02b-hub-api.md:28 says the hub assigns an id to every observed session.
resolution: GoalHooksState.trust is the tri-state HookTrustState (UNKNOWN, PENDING, TRUSTED, NOT_REQUIRED) with trust_approve_command; removed HOOK_EVENT_KIND_GOAL_WRITTEN and CONNECT_REASON_HUB_REQUESTED; added HarnessHookEvent.decision and harness_session_id on RespawnPane and EnsureWindow. The LogStreamKey item stays a doc note and belongs to theme D (dev-session-log-key).

title: Reused-session goals cannot get FLEET_GOAL_ID or the right cwd, so hooks, goal registry and adoption all break on the reuse path
evidence: 03c-goals.md:70-72 makes reusing an available_for_work session the preferred plan ('reuse (no new window)'); 03c-goals.md:87-91 says FLEET_GOAL_ID/FLEET_PANE_KEY are put in the pane environment by ensure_window, a step that is skipped on reuse (command_goal.proto:109-123 reuse_pane, in_session). 01d-goal-hooks.md:40-43 states Claude/Codex hooks gate on FLEET_GOAL_ID reaching hooks through the pane environment; a harness process already running cannot receive a new env var. W2 adoption/orphan detection (03-workflows.md:130-131, 03c-goals.md:243 PANE_LOST->RUNNING 'same FLEET_GOAL_ID') and snapshot.proto:126-128 TmuxPane.fleet_tags depend on the same tag. 01d-goal-hooks.md:44-49 (Muse registry keyed by worktree cwd) and 01d:263-267 (open question) never say what cwd a reused session has: the reused harness is sitting in whatever directory it was started in, not the new goal's worktree (WORKTREE_MODE_AGENT_ENSURES, command_goal.proto:20-26). In WORKTREE_MODE_REPO_DRIVER the goal starts in the main checkout, so registering that path makes every developer Muse session in the same checkout look like a fleet goal (Stop guard fights the developer). The registry itself is persisted nowhere: 03c-goals.md:341 says 'Nothing goal-specific on the agent beyond the command log' and the agent state dir lists in 03-workflows.md:51-53 and :297-304 omit it; no StartGoal step writes it (03c-goals.md:82-91); nothing releases it; Snapshot (snapshot.proto:329-371) cannot show it.
problem: The identity of a fleet goal on the machine is defined three incompatible ways (env var, cwd registry, session_id) and the registry has no lifecycle: no write step in StartGoal, no persistence entry, no release trigger, no rebuild rule after state-dir loss or re-enroll, no reconcile visibility on the wire. The reuse path (the main way to keep subscriptions busy) cannot satisfy any of the three as written.
fix: Decide that the agent goal registry is the single goal-identity mechanism for all harnesses, with FLEET_* env kept only as a bonus for new windows. Add register_goal to the StartGoal steps (03c:82-91), covering both new-window and reuse (bind to the pane's harness_session_id). Add the registry to the agent state dir lists (03-workflows.md:51-53, :297-304) and fix 03c:341. Define reuse eligibility: reuse only if the pane cwd is at or under the target workdir, otherwise SESSION_NOT_AVAILABLE; AGENT_ENSURES worktrees therefore need a new window. In REPO_DRIVER mode register by session_id and goal file, never by the shared main-checkout cwd. Release on MERGED/CLEARED/CLOSED and on PruneWorktree. Additive Snapshot.goal_registry[] lets the hub detect loss and rebuild.
verify: Confirmed. 03c-goals.md:87-91 puts FLEET_GOAL_ID/FLEET_PANE_KEY in the env only in ensure_window, which reuse skips (no reuse variant in command_goal.proto:109-123). 01d-goal-hooks.md:40-43 has Claude/Codex hooks gate on that pane env var, and a running harness cannot gain or replace an env var, so a reused pane keeps the previous goal's tag or none. 01d:44-49 says StartGoal writes a Muse worktree-path registry in the agent state dir, but 03c:82-91 has no registry step, 03c:341 says 'Nothing goal-specific on the agent beyond the command log', 03-workflows.md:51-53 and :297-304 omit it from the state dir lists, and nothing releases it or exposes it in snapshot.proto. 01d:263-267 only raises the cd-outside-worktree case, not what cwd a reused session has. ensure_worktree runs before pick_session (03c:82-91), so with AGENT_ENSURES the reused harness sits in another directory; 03-workflows.md:130-131 and 03c:265 (PANE_LOST/orphan detection) key on the same tag. Downgraded from blocker: nothing in the protos blocks implementation, the fix is additive, and without the Stop guard the W6 corrective nudge still covers a stopped goal, so this degrades v2 reuse rather than stopping it. It must be decided before the agent goal registry and hooks are built.
resolution: Same registry design as goal-binding-reused-pane: register_goal covers new-window and reuse, the registry is in the agent state dir lists (03-workflows, 03c), released on ReleaseGoal, pane exit and PruneWorktree, rebuilt from FLEET_GOAL_ID for new windows or by RegisterGoal for reused panes, and REPO_DRIVER registers by pane and session id, never the shared checkout path.

title: Developer interrupts and harness-side pauses have no wire representation and contradict W6's nudge rule
evidence: 01d-goal-hooks.md:23-24 and :116-127: hooks never resume a developer-interrupted goal, 'Nothing resumes automatically', the agent 'reports HarnessCondition (E12)' and the hub opens 'goal interrupted - resume?'. But HarnessConditionKind (harness.proto:199-213) has only PROVIDER_ERROR, RATE_LIMITED, USAGE_LIMIT, SIGN_IN_REQUIRED, NETWORK, OTHER; HookEventKind (events.proto:197-204) has no INTERRUPT although Codex and Muse fire Interrupt hooks (01d:31-35, E8 in 01-agent-capabilities.md:~249); GoalLineState (harness.proto:145-155) only mirrors the goal file; hub GoalPhase PAUSED is defined only for operator/review-loop/reserve (goal.proto:36-37, 03c-goals.md:259). W6 03c-goals.md:284-296 treats 'idle at ready prompt with WORKING line' as Stopped-without-DONE and sends the corrective nudge 'Your goal is still active. Continue...'; the only suppression is human_at_keyboard_until for 10 min (03c-goals.md:272-275). After 10 min the fleet would resume a goal the developer deliberately interrupted, and for Codex/Muse 'Goal paused' is not even a stop the goal file shows. 03c-goals.md:239-268 state diagram also has no LIMIT_WAIT or interrupted state although GoalPhase LIMIT_WAIT exists (goal.proto:41) and 02-contracts.md:361 defines it.
problem: The hub cannot distinguish 'harness stopped by accident' from 'goal paused/interrupted by a person' from 'goal achieved/cleared on screen' because only the goal file line is reported. W6 diagram is missing LIMIT_WAIT and any interrupted/paused-by-human transition.
fix: Additive: HARNESS_CONDITION_KIND_GOAL_INTERRUPTED (or an explicit paused-by-interrupt field on GoalState), plus HOOK_EVENT_KIND_INTERRUPT. In W6 add RUNNING->PAUSED{reason=interrupted} with no auto-nudge and no no-progress counting, and add LIMIT_WAIT entry and exit to the diagram. Keep human_at_keyboard_until as a secondary guard.
verify: Confirmed. 01d-goal-hooks.md:116-127 says the agent 'reports HarnessCondition (E12)' for an interrupt and the hub opens 'goal interrupted - resume?', but HarnessConditionKind (harness.proto:199-213) has no interrupt or pause kind. HookEventKind (events.proto:197-204) has no INTERRUPT, though raw_event_name (events.proto:~210) can carry it as a stopgap. GoalLineState (harness.proto:145-155) only mirrors the goal file. GoalPhase PAUSED (goal.proto:36-37) is for operator, review-loop and reserve only. W6 (03c:284-296) treats an idle ready prompt with a WORKING line as stopped and sends the nudge, suppressed only by the 10 min human_at_keyboard_until, so a deliberately paused Codex/Muse goal would be nudged. The W6 diagram (03c:239-268) has no LIMIT_WAIT state although GoalPhase LIMIT_WAIT exists (goal.proto:41) and 02-contracts.md:361-366 defines it.
resolution: GOAL_INTERRUPTED/GOAL_PAUSED conditions with pause_cause and HOOK_EVENT_KIND_INTERRUPT; 03c W6 diagram gains RUNNING to PAUSED (at the machine) and LIMIT_WAIT entry and exit, with no nudge and no no-progress counting while paused; human_at_keyboard_until is now fed by PaneInput as a secondary guard.

title: No wire signal for keystrokes or ready-prompt state on goal panes, but W6 depends on both
evidence: Availability (harness.proto:133-142) and E11 (01-agent-capabilities.md:~268-272) define idle as 'ready pattern showing, NO active goal, no output or input'; on a goal pane idle is therefore always false, so AvailabilityChanged (events.proto:229-238) never fires with reason 'keystroke' there (no idle transition to report). W6 still needs it: 03c-goals.md:272-275 human_at_keyboard_until is 'after an AvailabilityChanged{reason=keystroke}', 03c-goals.md:367 and 03-workflows.md:331 (replay case) and ui-contract-map.md:104 (typing banner). W6 also needs 'harness ready pattern showing for longer than idle_threshold' (03c-goals.md:284-287) and 'waits for ready (HarnessReady or ready pattern)' after Interrupt (03c-goals.md:319-321). HarnessReady (events.proto:188-194) is a v2 edge event, not in Snapshot or TmuxPane (snapshot.proto:115-140), ActivityTransition (events.proto:163-169) is output activity only, and TmuxPane has last_output_at but no last_input_at.
problem: Two level-triggered facts the nudge, pause/resume and typing-banner logic need are not carried at all (keystroke time, ready-pattern showing), and after a reconnect the snapshot cannot rebuild them because the only carrier is a droppable-by-ring edge event.
fix: Additive: TmuxPane.last_input_at and TmuxPane.ready_pattern_showing, plus a coalesced input_activity event (or let AvailabilityChanged fire on goal panes with a human_input flag). Define HarnessReady as a level fact with a snapshot field. Update E11 and 03c wording so the human-at-keyboard rule names its actual source.
verify: Confirmed. harness.proto:133-142 defines Availability.idle as ready pattern showing, no active goal, no output or input, so on a goal pane idle is always false and AvailabilityChanged (events.proto:229-238) has no idle transition to fire 'keystroke' on. W6 still depends on it (03c:272-275, 03-workflows.md:331, ui-contract-map.md:104). TmuxPane (snapshot.proto:115-140) has last_output_at but no last_input_at and no ready-pattern flag. HarnessReady (events.proto:188-194) is an edge event only, not in Snapshot, so after a reconnect the 'ready for longer than idle_threshold' fact (03c:284-287) and the interrupt-then-wait-ready step (03c:319-321) cannot be rebuilt. Real contract gap before v2 goal handling.
resolution: TmuxPane.last_input_time and ready_pattern_showing are level facts in the snapshot; PaneInput and HarnessReady{showing} (both COALESCE) carry the changes, so a reconnect rebuilds them. E7, E11 and a new E13 in 01 and 02-contracts name the real source.

title: Per-harness goal-control actions (pause, resume, continue) live in hub code, not on the wire; LIMIT_WAIT resume cites a probe that did not cover it
evidence: 01b-harness-commands.md:116-117 says 'the adapter records which subcommands each harness version supports; the hub never sends one that isn't listed', but HarnessInfo (snapshot.proto:82-108) and CatalogEntry (harness.proto:32-38) carry only slash-command names and classes, no subcommands or resume style. 03c-goals.md:301-303 and :317-330 and 02-contracts.md:361-366 hard-code the table in the hub: Claude resume = SendKeys 'continue', Codex/Muse = RunHarnessCommand '/goal resume', Claude pause = Interrupt; hub goal.proto:1-4 says the hub translates intent per harness. Harness is an open extension string (ids.proto:121-125) and OpenCode has no /goal (01b:71-72). 02-contracts.md:365 justifies the limit-resume actions with '01b probes, 2026-10-02', but those probes (01b:94-100) cover interrupt, not usage-limit state. GOAL_SUBCOMMAND_UNSUPPORTED (status.proto:143-145) is only discovered by sending. HarnessCondition.resets_at (screen.proto:61-64) is a bare Timestamp: unlike ResetTime it carries no original text/timezone and unset is not specified.
problem: The hub cannot be harness-agnostic: adding the OpenCode or a fourth adapter requires hub code changes. 'Never sends an unlisted subcommand' is unenforceable. Limit-resume behaviour is unverified. Unresolvable resets_at has no fallback.
fix: Doc fixes: reword 01b:116-117 to say the hub's per-harness table is the source until a goal_control capability exists; mark limit-resume per harness as untested (open question, probe it); specify resets_at unset means the hub re-checks the condition every 10 min and on the next probe reading, capped at the weekly reset. Optional additive HarnessInfo.goal_control {pause, resume} if a fourth harness is expected.
verify: Partly confirmed. 01b-harness-commands.md:116-117 says the adapter records supported subcommands and the hub never sends one that isn't listed, but HarnessInfo (snapshot.proto:82-108) and CatalogEntry (harness.proto:32-38) carry only command names and classes, so that guarantee is unenforceable and the per-harness table lives in the hub (03c:301-330, 02-contracts.md:361-366); GOAL_SUBCOMMAND_UNSUPPORTED (status.proto:305) is found only by sending. Confirmed that 02-contracts.md:365 cites '01b probes, 2026-10-02' for limit-resume, but the 01b probe table (01b:~88-95) covers interrupt, not usage-limit state. HarnessCondition.resets_at (screen.proto:~72) is a bare Timestamp with no fallback when unset ('if shown'). Overstated: the harness set is closed (Claude, Codex, Muse; OpenCode has no /goal) and any new harness already needs an agent adapter, so the hub-code-change argument is weak for v1/v2; no blocker.
resolution: GoalControl on HarnessInfo and MachineHarness is the per-harness account (the optional goal_control capability); limit resume is marked unprobed (limit_resume_verified false) in 01b, 02-contracts and 02h, and an unresolvable resets_time means a 10 minute re-check capped at the weekly reset.

title: StartGoal composite omits steps and reason codes the specs require (register, goal file, model/effort/clear, startup prompts)
evidence: 03c-goals.md:82-91 lists seven steps (preflight, ensure_worktree, pick_session, ensure_window, wait_ready, type_goal, confirm_goal_file). Missing: the goal-file write that 01d-goal-hooks.md:103-109 says the agent does just before type_goal; the registry write (see reuse finding); /model and /effort selection and the destructive /clear for GoalSpec.model/effort/fresh_context (command_goal.proto:56-65, 02-contracts.md:350-356). CommandProgress.step is a free string (command.proto:96-99) with only an example list, yet the hub's retry policy is keyed by step and reason (03c-goals.md:117-127). status.proto has TRUST_PROMPT_SEEN (:142) but no code for the other startup prompts the adapter must classify and never answer (01b-harness-commands.md:103-108: Codex 'update available', login, release notes; the probe's blind '1'+Enter ran brew upgrade), and no code for 'model/effort not accepted by this harness'. These fall back to READY_TIMEOUT or INVALID_ARGUMENT, which 03c-goals.md:122-123 retries on a new window, repeating the same prompt.
problem: Step list, step_count and failure taxonomy are incomplete, so durable (do not retry) vs transient (retry) cannot be keyed correctly, and update/login prompts at start are retried instead of triaged.
fix: Freeze a closed step vocabulary in 02-contracts.md with stable step_count per harness (preflight, ensure_worktree, pick_session, ensure_window, register_goal, select_model, select_effort, clear_context, wait_ready, write_goal_file, type_goal, confirm_goal_file). Add reason codes STARTUP_PROMPT_SEEN (metadata kind: trust|update|login|release_notes; keep TRUST_PROMPT_SEEN), MODEL_NOT_AVAILABLE and EFFORT_NOT_SUPPORTED in the 300 range, and treat update/login as durable per (machine, harness) in W5 with a triage item instead of a retry.
verify: Confirmed. The StartGoal sequence (03c-goals.md:25-50) and step list (:82-91) have seven steps and omit the goal-file write that 01d-goal-hooks.md:103-109 puts just before type_goal, the registry write, and the model/effort/clear steps for GoalSpec.model/effort/fresh_context (command_goal.proto:56-65, 02-contracts.md:350-356). CommandProgress.step is a free string with an example list (command.proto:~92-99), while the hub retry policy (03c:117-127) is keyed by step and reason. status.proto has TRUST_PROMPT_SEEN (304) but no code for update, login or release-notes startup prompts that 01b-harness-commands.md:103-108 says the adapter must classify and send to Triage (the Codex probe's blind '1'+Enter ran brew upgrade), and no code for model or effort not accepted. Such failures fall back to READY_TIMEOUT, which 03c:122-123 retries once on a new window, repeating the same prompt.
resolution: Closed 14-step vocabulary with constant step_count in command_goal.proto, CommandProgress and 02h; new reasons STARTUP_PROMPT_SEEN (metadata kind trust, update, login, release_notes; TRUST_PROMPT_SEEN kept), MODEL_NOT_AVAILABLE, EFFORT_NOT_SUPPORTED, GOAL_FILE_WRITE_FAILED in the 300 range; update and login prompts are durable per (machine, harness) and raise triage (03c).

title: SLOTS_FULL and max_active enforcement have no owner: agent 'does not compute slots' but a preflight code and a local ceiling assume it does
evidence: 01-agent-capabilities.md:~128 'The agent does not compute free slots'; 03e-settings-and-drift.md:57-58 'max_active/max_total are hub-side limits the agent only echoes'; hub goal.proto:189 lists SLOTS_FULL as a hub-side refusal. But REASON_CODE_SLOTS_FULL sits in the agent preflight range (status.proto:90), command_goal.proto:101-104 gives SLOTS_FULL as an agent PreflightFailure example, 02-contracts.md:314-318 lists preflight 13-15 under REJECTED_BY_POLICY, and 03e:37-40 applies tighten-only min(hub, local) to max_active so a local policy ceiling is meaningful only if somebody enforces it. 03c-goals.md:67-69 compares PaneCounts.goal_panes_by_state (keyed by GoalLineState, agent.proto:203-205) with hub phases, which have no 1:1 mapping (STOPPED, COOLDOWN, PAUSED, LIMIT_WAIT).
problem: If the agent never emits SLOTS_FULL the local max_active ceiling is unenforced; if it does, 'agent does not compute slots' is wrong. The heartbeat mismatch test is not well-defined.
fix: Decide: the agent enforces its effective max_active/max_total at StartGoal from its own GoalState counts as defense in depth (SLOTS_FULL, REJECTED_BY_POLICY), while the hub schedules from its table. Define active and total by aggregate and compare only those two aggregates against PaneCounts. Fix the wording in 01 and 03e.
verify: Confirmed doc contradiction. 01-agent-capabilities.md:128 says the agent does not compute free slots, and 03e-settings-and-drift.md:57-58 says max_active/max_total are hub-side limits the agent only echoes, yet 03e:37-40 lists max_active/max_total under tighten-only min(hub, local), so a local ceiling is meaningless unless the agent enforces it. SLOTS_FULL sits in the agent preflight range (status.proto:90), is an agent PreflightFailure example (command_goal.proto:101), and 02-contracts.md:318 lists it as an agent preflight passing reason, while the hub-side list (hub goal.proto:~189) also uses it. 03c:66-69 compares PaneCounts.goal_panes_by_state (keyed by GoalLineState, agent.proto:203-205) with hub counts, but hub phases map non-1:1 (STOPPED, COOLDOWN, PAUSED, LIMIT_WAIT), so the mismatch test is undefined.
resolution: The hub owns max_active enforcement (SLOTS_FULL is a hub reason in hub_checks); the agent has a local safety cap with REASON_CODE_AGENT_GOAL_CAP_REACHED and sends exactly two aggregates, PaneCounts.goals_active and goals_total, which the hub compares for slot_mismatch (02h, 01, 03c).

title: A person interrupting or pausing a goal at the machine (owner-paused) has no wire event, condition kind, phase or triage kind, and 03c contradicts 01d; PAUSED has no reason
evidence: docs/specs/01d-goal-hooks.md:124-127: 'An interrupt is the developer's decision... agent reports HarnessCondition... hub opens Triage item goal interrupted -- resume?... Nothing resumes automatically.' But api/fleet/type/v1/harness.proto:199-213 HarnessConditionKind has no INTERRUPTED; api/fleet/agent/v1/events.proto:197-204 HookEventKind has no INTERRUPT (01d:60-63 says Codex and Muse have an Interrupt hook); api/fleet/hub/v1/triage.proto:20-40 TriageKind has no interrupted or owner-paused kind although docs/design.md:198 lists an 'owner paused' chip. 03c:284-288 treats ActivityTransition{IDLE} on a WORKING goal as 'stopped without DONE' and 03c:367 suppresses nudges only for 10 min after a keystroke (human_at_keyboard_until), after which 03c:290-296 types 'Your goal is still active. Continue...'. api/fleet/hub/v1/goal.proto:36 GOAL_PHASE_PAUSED covers 'operator, review-loop cap, reserve' only; 03c:300,331 write PAUSED{review_loop} and reserve pauses but Goal has no field for the reason.
problem: A developer pressing Esc on a goal pane (Claude shows 'Interrupted', Codex 'Goal paused', Muse 'goal paused by interrupt') will be classified STOPPED, then auto-nudged back to work after 10 minutes, overriding the owner's decision and contradicting 01d. The hub also cannot tell its own pause (which must auto-resume: reserve resets, review loop) from an owner or operator pause (which must never auto-resume): 03c:256 only has 'PAUSED --> RUNNING: operator resume', and 03c:331 says reserve pauses resume 'when the bucket resets' with no trigger or timestamp field. After an operator resumes a review_loop pause, review_rounds is still >= 3 (03c:300), so the cap re-fires immediately; no baseline field exists.
fix: Additive: HARNESS_CONDITION_KIND_INTERRUPTED (with goal_id) and HOOK_EVENT_KIND_INTERRUPT; TRIAGE_KIND_GOAL_PAUSED; Goal.pause_reason enum {OPERATOR, OWNER_AT_MACHINE, REVIEW_LOOP, RESERVE, LIMIT} plus Goal.paused_by and a review_rounds baseline. In 03c: INTERRUPTED on a goal pane -> PAUSED{OWNER_AT_MACHINE}, exempt from the corrective nudge, never auto-resumed; RESERVE pauses auto-resume at the deciding bucket resets_at; review-loop cap compares review_rounds minus baseline.
verify: Confirmed. 01d-goal-hooks.md:124-127 says the agent reports a HarnessCondition for an interrupt and the hub opens a 'goal interrupted' triage item, nothing resumes automatically. But HarnessConditionKind (harness.proto:~199-213) has no INTERRUPTED, HookEventKind (events.proto:~197-204) has no INTERRUPT although 01d:34-35 lists the Interrupt hook, and TriageKind (triage.proto:20-40) has no interrupted/paused kind although design.md:198 lists an 'owner paused' chip. 03c:284-289 treats IDLE on a WORKING goal as 'stopped without DONE', suppressed only by human_at_keyboard_until (10 min, 03c:273,367), then 03c:290-296 types the corrective 'Your goal is still active. Continue' nudge, which overrides a deliberate Esc. PAUSED (03c:255-256) has only 'operator resume', no reason field on Goal, and 03c:332 'resume when the bucket resets' has no trigger/timestamp. review_loop pause (03c:301-303) keys on ChangeRequest.review_rounds >= 3 with no baseline, so it re-fires after an operator resume.
resolution: Hub: GoalPauseReason (OPERATOR, OWNER_AT_MACHINE, REVIEW_LOOP, RESERVE), GoalStatus.pause_reason, paused_by, review_rounds_baseline and auto_resume_time, TRIAGE_KIND_GOAL_PAUSED. Agent: GOAL_INTERRUPTED and GOAL_PAUSED conditions with pause_cause. 03c: owner pauses are never nudged or auto-resumed, RESERVE resumes at auto_resume_time, the review cap compares against the baseline. LIMIT is not a pause reason: it is the LIMIT_WAIT phase.

title: GoalSpec.model/effort/fresh_context have no composite steps, failure reasons, role path or auto-dispatch defaults; per-model pacing has no input when model is empty
evidence: api/fleet/agent/v1/command_goal.proto:56-65 (model, effort, fresh_context) and api/fleet/agent/v1/command.proto:96-97 CommandProgress.step list; docs/specs/03c-goals.md:84-91 composite steps are preflight, ensure_worktree, pick_session, ensure_window, wait_ready, type_goal, confirm_goal_file only; api/fleet/type/v1/status.proto:68-168 has FRESH_CONTEXT_NOT_ALLOWED but no reason for model or effort unavailable; docs/specs/01b-harness-commands.md:38,44 /model and /effort are SESSION class 'operator role', /clear is DESTRUCTIVE 'local approval or explicit owner action'; status.proto:203-210 Role.SCHEDULER has no documented class permissions (grep: only 02b:154); docs/specs/03b-usage-and-sync.md:86-88 pacing uses 'the per-model bucket of the goal's model'; api/fleet/hub/v1/session.proto:41 Pane.model is OpenCode-only.
problem: The typed steps /model, /effort and /clear (and their picker-UI handling, success detection and rollback) are not in the composite, so step_count, retry policy and UNKNOWN_OUTCOME behaviour are undefined for them. Auto-dispatch runs as SCHEDULER; whether that role may type SESSION-class commands, and how a DESTRUCTIVE /clear is approved when nobody is at the machine (AWAITING_LOCAL_CONFIRM would stall a dispatch), is not stated. The planner never says when auto-dispatch sets fresh_context, model or effort (a reused session after MERGED carries the previous goal's context; WorkItem.size S/M/L, work.proto:48-49, is set by no one). When model is empty ('leave as is') the hub cannot know which per-model bucket (weekly_fable) applies, so the exhaustion rule at 03b:86-88 is undefined.
fix: Doc-level: add optional steps set_model, set_effort, clear_context between wait_ready and type_goal with additive reasons MODEL_UNAVAILABLE/EFFORT_UNSUPPORTED; state SCHEDULER may use GOAL and SESSION classes and fresh_context only in fleet-started sessions; rule: auto-dispatch into a reused session sets fresh_context=true; have StartGoalResult echo the effective model so pacing uses the right bucket, or evaluate only weekly_all plus the harness default model's bucket when model is empty.
verify: Confirmed but smaller than claimed. 03c:82-91 composite steps omit set_model/set_effort/clear_context, and status.proto has only REASON_CODE_FRESH_CONTEXT_NOT_ALLOWED (:148), no model/effort reasons. However CommandProgress.step is a free string ('e.g.', command.proto:~93) so adding steps is non-breaking, and 02-contracts.md:350-360 plus command_goal.proto:56-65 already limit /clear to fleet-started sessions, which answers the DESTRUCTIVE-approval concern (no local confirm is involved). Genuine gaps: SCHEDULER role's allowed classes are undocumented (status.proto:209), planner never says when auto-dispatch sets fresh_context/model/effort, and with empty model the per-model bucket in 03b:86-88 is undefined (Pane.model is OpenCode-only, session.proto:~37).
resolution: Steps set_model, set_effort and clear_context added with MODEL_NOT_AVAILABLE and EFFORT_NOT_SUPPORTED; the scheduler may run them inside StartGoal with local approval asked once before step 1 (02g, 02h); auto-dispatch into a reused pane sets fresh_context; StartGoalResult.model and effort let pacing use the right bucket, with weekly_all plus the default model's bucket until then.

title: Session reuse contradicts agent-ensured worktrees (harness cwd cannot change), the hub cannot see a pane's workdir, and prune is ordered before KillWindow
evidence: docs/specs/03c-goals.md:84-91 ensure_worktree runs before pick_session; :86-87 reuse of an available session; :233 and :311-316 'PruneWorktree, KillWindow'; api/fleet/agent/v1/snapshot.proto:111-130 TmuxPane has no cwd/workdir/repo; docs/specs/01d-goal-hooks.md:56-59 Muse goal registry keys on the worktree path a StartGoal records and a cwd at or under it; api/fleet/hub/v1/goal.proto:141-145 GoalPlacement.reuse_session; docs/specs/01-agent-capabilities.md:293-304 (E11 reuse).
problem: A harness process is started in one directory. If the agent creates a fresh worktree for the next goal (AGENT_ENSURES) and then reuses the idle session, the harness is still in the old worktree/branch, the registry path for Muse hooks is wrong, the goal file lands elsewhere, and the new branch is not the one being worked. Reuse is only coherent when the session sits in the repo checkout and the repo's driver (REPO_DRIVER) makes worktrees, or the session was started in the target worktree. The planner (03c:67-71) cannot filter reusable sessions by repo, directory or profile because TmuxPane exposes none of them, so it reserves a session blind and relies on SESSION_NOT_AVAILABLE. Separately, the diagram prunes the worktree before killing the window, removing the directory under a live harness; and the reused-session path leaves the old worktree unpruned forever ('A session that was reused is left alone').
fix: Add TmuxPane.workdir (Workdir{repo, relative_path}) derived by the agent. Rule in 03c: reuse is eligible only when pane.workdir.repo == goal repo and (worktree_mode == REPO_DRIVER, or the session was started in the target worktree); otherwise always ensure_window. Order cleanup KillWindow then PruneWorktree and prune the previous goal's agent-created worktree when its session is reused.
verify: Confirmed. TmuxPane (snapshot.proto:111-130) and hub Pane (session.proto:19-40) carry no workdir/repo, so the planner (03c:67-71) cannot filter reusable sessions by repo and relies on SESSION_NOT_AVAILABLE. 03c:84-91 runs ensure_worktree (AGENT_ENSURES) before pick_session, and a reused harness process keeps its original cwd, so reuse in AGENT_ENSURES mode lands the goal in the old worktree/branch (also breaking the Muse registry path in 01d:56-59). 03c:233 and :311-316 list PruneWorktree before KillWindow, and :316 'A session that was reused is left alone' leaves the previous worktree unpruned.
resolution: A reused pane keeps its directory: no ensure_worktree, the goal starts a new branch in place (prepare_branch); the planner filters by TmuxPane.workdir.repo. Cleanup is KillWindow then PruneWorktree, with new REASON_CODE_WORKTREE_IN_USE for a worktree a live pane works in (02h, 03c).

title: For REPO_DRIVER goals (eshu, the primary repo) the hub never learns the branch or worktree, breaking CR lookup by head_ref and the one-agent-per-branch rule
evidence: api/fleet/agent/v1/snapshot.proto:194-215 GoalState has goal_file ('relative to the worktree') but no branch, workdir or worktree path; :218-232 BranchState.goal_id and :241-251 RepoCheckout.goal_id are 'set when the worktree was created by fleet' (agent/v1/snapshot.proto RepoCheckout comment); docs/specs/03c-goals.md:84-85 'eshu's driver creates its own, so REPO_DRIVER starts in the main checkout'; docs/specs/03b-usage-and-sync.md:243-246 CR lookup uses BranchState.branch; docs/specs/03f-hub-internals.md goals unique (repo, branch); docs/design.md:279 'One agent per PR branch'; api/fleet/hub/v1/goal.proto:92 Goal.branch has no stated source.
problem: With a driver-created worktree no BranchState carries goal_id, so Goal.branch stays empty, the head_ref GraphQL batch cannot target the goal's CR, and unique (repo, branch) cannot be enforced. The fallback (03b:269 linked_work_items on any CR updated since dispatch) works for issue goals but not for routines or change-request take-overs, and it is slow (60 s poll) with false matches when two issues are in flight. The Muse registry (01d) and PruneWorktree ('agent-created worktrees only') have the same blind spot.
fix: Add GoalState.workdir and GoalState.branch, filled by the agent from the goal file's directory (git rev-parse) and re-sent on change; set BranchState.goal_id whenever a fleet goal file lives in the worktree regardless of creator; hub maps it to Goal.branch and the CR sync keys on it. Document that PruneWorktree never touches a driver-created worktree.
verify: Confirmed. GoalState (snapshot.proto:194-215) has goal_file relative to the worktree but no branch/workdir; RepoCheckout.goal_id is 'set when the worktree was created by fleet' (snapshot.proto:~236), and 03c:84-85 says REPO_DRIVER starts in the main checkout with the driver creating its own worktree, so no BranchState is tied to the goal. 03b:243-246 finds the CR via BranchState.branch, 03f:104 requires unique (repo, branch), design.md:279 requires one agent per branch, yet Goal.branch (goal.proto:33) has no documented source (ui-contract-map.md:109 only reads it). The 03b:269 linked_work_items fallback covers issue goals but not routines or CR take-overs. Affects eshu, the primary repo.
resolution: GoalState gains worktree_path and branch (from the goal file's directory, re-sent on change) so Goal.status.branch, head_ref lookup and the one-agent-per-branch rule work for REPO_DRIVER goals; BranchState.goal_id is set whenever a fleet goal file lives in the worktree; PruneWorktree never touches a driver-created worktree (02h).

title: No event for mutable pane/window/session attributes, and internal tmux sessions (attach view, probe server) have no hub treatment
evidence: agent/v1/events.proto:117-123 (ChangeKind: CREATED, RENAMED, CLOSED only), :140-151 (WindowEvent, PaneCreated). The Event oneof (events.proto:40-102) has no pane-changed kind. agent/v1/snapshot.proto:115-140 (TmuxPane mutable fields: current_command, harness, active, cols/rows, log_capture, window.active/index), :154-174 (attached_clients). hub/v1/session.proto:19-44,72-92 expose them. Snapshot is sent only on connect or SnapshotRequest (agent/v1/snapshot.proto:322-326; docs/specs/02-contracts.md:106,123). docs/specs/ui-contract-map.md:99 requires Pane.active and current_command. For internal sessions: agent/v1/snapshot.proto:167-168 (`attach_view`), :177-186 (TmuxServer kind PROBE); hub Session has no such field (session.proto:72-92) and ListSessions filters omit server (session.proto:109-111); grep finds no hub rule excluding them.
problem: When a developer starts `claude` in an existing shell pane, `Pane.harness`, `current_command` and `active` change, and no event carries it. The hub's Session view is stale until a reconnect, and the harness-dependent logic (availability, usage passive reads, prompt detection UI) works from stale data. This is week-one v1 read-only tmux observation. Grouped attach-view sessions share windows with the real session, so the same PaneKey is listed under two sessions, and fleet-probe sessions would appear in the Session list and counts, with no stated filter.
fix: Add CHANGE_KIND_UPDATED and a `PaneChanged` event (full TmuxPane, `coalesce_key = pane:<key>`, class COALESCE), or add a pane-level update to WindowEvent. State in 02-contracts and 03d that the hub never materialises `attach_view` sessions as Sessions or counts them in `attached_clients`, and either hides TMUX_SERVER_KIND_PROBE or adds `Session.internal` and a `server` filter. Additive.
verify: critic (verified in files by the critic)
resolution: CHANGE_KIND_UPDATED and Event.pane_changed (PaneChanged, COALESCE) for mutable pane attributes; TmuxSession.internal marks attach views and probe-server sessions, which the hub never materialises as Sessions, lists panes of or counts (02h, 03d, 02-contracts E1).

title: How the agent derives RepoRef from a checkout (remote choice, forks, multiple checkouts, code_host) is unspecified
evidence: agent/v1/snapshot.proto:232-246 (RepoCheckout has a single `repo`, no remote name or url); docs/specs/01-agent-capabilities.md:368-370 (H1: 'repo reference' only); type/v1/work.proto:12-25 (RepoRef.code_host is a hub-assigned IntegrationId inside a type the agent also fills and receives in Workdir); agent/v1/command_goal.proto:140-150 (EnsureWorktree addresses 'the main checkout'). grep for remote/origin/fork in docs: only ADR 0012:36 'SSH and HTTPS remotes normalize'.
problem: A checkout with `origin` = fork and `upstream` = the watched repo, a checkout with no remote, a repo moved or renamed on the host, or two checkouts of the same repo on one machine all have no defined result. Push-access and ForgeCliStatus.access are per repo, so picking the wrong remote produces false PUSH_ACCESS_MISSING or the wrong work item to repo match. The agent cannot know `code_host` ids, so proto equality of RepoRef across agent and hub will differ unless code_host is excluded from identity.
fix: Specify in 01/02: the remote used (default `origin`, overridable by a local policy setting), reporting of all remotes (or a `remote_name` plus normalized url on RepoCheckout), the rule for duplicate checkouts (prefer the allowed root listed first or the one named in Workdir), and that RepoRef identity is (host, path) only with `code_host` hub-filled and ignored for equality. Additive.
verify: critic (verified in files by the critic)
resolution: 02h, Repo identity: remote is origin unless local policy names another, RepoCheckout.remote_name and remotes[] (GitRemote, no URLs) report all remotes and the fork case, normalization rules, duplicate checkout choice, and RepoRef identity is (host, path) only with code_host hub-filled and ignored for equality (comment on RepoRef).

title: Opaque ids are used as tmux names, env values, file paths and resource keys with no format rule; StartGoal's new-session name is ambiguous
evidence: agent/v1/command_goal.proto:113-114 ('empty = new session named by the hub in spec.session_id'; StartGoal has no name field) vs agent/v1/command_tmux.proto:67 (names must match [a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,31}) and :17-35. type/v1/ids.proto:45-53 (SessionId and GoalId go into FLEET_SESSION_ID and FLEET_GOAL_ID). hub/v1/settings.proto:49-50 (resource id 'group/<label>' with labels as free strings up to 256 bytes). docs/specs/03d-triage-sessions-logs.md:287 (log files keyed by session).
problem: Nothing defines id generation (ULID, length, charset). A session id used as the tmux session name must satisfy the 32-character name regex, and ids end up in environment values, file names and `group/<label>` keys that break if a label contains '/'. Developers will make different choices in the hub and agent in week one.
fix: Add an ids rule to 02-contracts: all hub-assigned ids are lowercase Crockford ULID or a stated prefix plus 26 chars, [a-z0-9-] only, at most 32 chars. Give StartGoal an explicit `session_name` (or state that the name is derived from the id and window template). Restrict group labels to the same charset. Additive.
verify: critic (verified in files by the critic)
resolution: ids.proto header: hub-assigned ids are 1 to 32 characters of [a-z0-9-] (lowercase ULID), user-chosen names that land in tmux names, env values, paths or group keys are [a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,31}; PrincipalId is the documented exception. A new StartGoal session is named spec.session_id.value (02h, 02e).
